Header: Phytophthora infestans Chiwawu cha mu tomato, Kachewere, Mbatatesi

Prevention: Plant certified disease- free seed that is clean of the pathogen.
Make sure seed tubers are free from dark lesions.
Avoid planting near other solanaceous crops that are alternative hosts to the pathogen.
Bury potato waste 2 m deep to dispose of the pathogen.
Rotate with non-host crops 2-3 years and use tolerant varieties.
Ensure good drainage and good air movement.
Remove other sources of inoculum such as crop debris, harvested infected potato, volunteer plants.
Waste potatoes can be fed to animals.
Monitoring: Follow weather forecasting to determine the favourable conditions for the disease and then consider using fungicide treatment as a preventative measure.
Monitor plants every week for symptoms.
Monitor more often when it is wet and humid and on the windward side of the field where moisture is likely to persist.
The disease attacks stems, leaves and tubers.
Look for early symptoms on leaves which are small, pale-green water- soaked spots.
The spots grow and turn brown/black and may have yellow halos.
Lesions spread rapidly at 15-20°C in humid conditions.
There may be white sporulation on the underside of the leaves.
Black greasy lesions may appear on the petioles and stems, girdling of the stem can kill the plant.
Infected potato tubers have wet and dry rot.
Apply controls when first symptoms are seen as this disease spreads very rapidly.
Fungicides can also be used as a preventative measure.
Direct Control: Rogue out plants showing severe symptoms of disease to prevent spread to other plants and destroy by burying or burning.
Slash and destroy foliage in an infected field 1 week before harvest to reduce infecting tubers.
